neet_phy_u07_t11_2.working: Heat lost by block = heat gained by water: 200(0.25)(100 − T) = 200(1)(T − 20). This gives 5000 − 50T = 200T − 4000, so 250T = 9000 and T = 36°C.

neet_phy_u07_t11_3.working: Water cooling from 30°C to 0°C releases 200 × 30 = 6000 cal. Melting all the ice needs 100 × 80 = 8000 cal. Since 6000 < 8000, only part of the ice melts and the mixture stays at 0°C.

neet_phy_u07_t11_4.working: Isothermal: heat flows with no temperature change, so C is infinite (II). Adiabatic: no heat flows, so C is zero (III). Cp − Cv = R (I). Water: 1 cal/g°C (IV). So A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

neet_phy_u07_t11_5.working: A is true: water equivalent = mc/c_w. B is true: calorimetry rests on energy conservation. C is true: ice is about 0.5 cal/g°C. D is false: for an ideal gas Cp > Cv. E is false: heat for unit mass is specific heat, not heat capacity. So A, B and C only.
